title: Affirming the consequent is a valid inference
statement: For all propositions p and q: if (p implies q) holds and q holds, then p holds. THIS PROPOSITION IS FALSE; the fact is recorded with status `refuted` and carries the countermodel.

evidence.supports: p := false, q := true satisfies the negation of the proposition, so the proposition is not a tautology
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14: the file asserts the NEGATION of formal.statement and the solver reported `sat` with `kind=sat-model certified=1 arena=ok`. `arena=ok` is Evidence::check replaying the model against a fresh parse of the file -- the model is evaluated against the original assertions, not against the lowered form. The witness is p := false, q := true: then (p implies q) is true and q is true while p is false. Independently cross-checked: `z3 -smt2` on the same file also reports `sat`.

notes: The only `refuted` fact in this batch, and the reason the status exists. It is the converse of F:modus-ponens-valid and the negation-free shadow of F:contraposition, and one two-line countermodel separates it from both. Note the asymmetry in cost that this fact makes visible: refuting a universally quantified propositional claim needs one assignment, while establishing one needs the whole truth table -- which is why `sat` evidence is a replayable witness and `unsat` evidence is a certificate.
